sections.title: Intro
sections.intro: Jackson Heights, in northwest Queens, is among the most culturally diverse neighborhoods in the world, yet it has some of the least public open space per resident in New York City.

sections.title: Phase 1
sections.intro: In 1909 the Queensboro Corporation laid a rigid orthogonal grid over the area and gave every block an interior garden.

slides.title: The Street Grid
slides.body: The grid has 1,001 mapped street segments with an average width of 32.6 feet.

slides.title: Broadway: Breaking the Grid
slides.body: Almost every street runs at a strict right angle, except Broadway, which cuts diagonally and leaves irregular lots along its edge.

sections.title: Shaping Jackson Heights
sections.intro: The city shapes the community. The community reshapes the city. Planned for a community. Reshaped by the people.
